input.content:
Six weeks ago, three of us shipped Skycast 1.0, a 7-day forecast app for Android and iOS. Here is what the numbers taught us.

Two weeks before launch we put a beta in front of 40 users. They surfaced 11 bugs, and we fixed 9 before 1.0. That single decision moved our crash rate from 4% of sessions in the beta down to 0.5% after launch, largely by killing a background refresh that misbehaved on low memory.

Performance mattered just as much. Caching the last forecast on the device cut cold start from 3.2 seconds to 1.1 seconds. Users notice a second.

The hardest call was cutting hourly radar maps. They ate a third of our design time, yet only 2 of 40 beta users ever opened them. Shipping less felt better than shipping late.

Six weeks in: 4.6 stars from 310 ratings. Top request is a widget, and it is next.

One habit I would repeat on any team: a weekly 20-minute demo to everyone. It caught two forecast-unit misunderstandings before they reached users.

# Skycast 1.4.0

Released 22 September 2026

## What's new

- **Home-screen widget.** See today's high, low and chance of rain without opening the app.
- **Pick your own units.** Choose Celsius or Fahrenheit independently of your phone's region.

## Fixes

- Temperature unit no longer stays wrong after you switch regions — the change now takes effect immediately, no restart needed.
- Forecasts for locations near the international date line now show the correct day.

Thanks for using Skycast. Keep the feedback coming.
